text: Article · research post · Rikiya Takehi's blog (rikiyat.github.io) · updated 12 November 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, Omar Khattab (MIT CSAIL) · published 2 November 2026 In one line: In one blog post with complete released logs, mostly single runs, GPT-6 Astra named what small networks (17K to 24K weights) were trained for from their raw weights with no tools, wrote MinAtar policies from all-zero weights that beat PPO at 100M steps in all three games (at 500M steps only in Breakout), and, with a Python kernel over Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and 50 forward passes on practice problems, made a rank-one edit to 131,072 weights (0.016%) that cut thinking loops and raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% in a looping-prone setting (thinking on, 32,768 tokens).
